entries.capability: Session bearer exposure through PostgreSQL session settings
entries.defect: The raw server-held session bearer was placed in a transaction-local PostgreSQL setting so definer predicates can hash it in-database. The pg-session path sent the caller's long-lived cookie as a bind parameter (TypeScript org-binding and the Django canonical context). REMEDIATED IN CODE: both writers now validate the cookie and forward only a 30-second single-purpose bridge token, revoked when the callback or request ends. Proven by the unit test, the native identity suite on the pinned local pgvector image (17/17, with new assertions) and all 25 bootstrap-v2 files including the Django framework native proof (636 tests). REMAINING: a bridge outlives revocation of its parent session by at most 30 seconds (no parent link in the definer predicates; closing it needs a governed predicate migration); deployment log controls (log_parameter_max_length, log_statement) are an unverified operations gate; not a staging isolation pass.
entries.securityImplications: A credential in a server setting can leak into logs or be read by a same-session query.
entries.requiredImplementation: Apply the deployment log controls and stop passing the long-lived cookie (mint a short-lived bridge session or bind a derived proof) through the governed migration lineage, proven on PostgreSQL 15 and 16. CONTINUATION 7: Drizzle bind-parameter errors could carry the bridge token; binding failures are now reduced to their SQLSTATE (lib/db/binding-error.ts). New ratchets pin the files allowed to touch app.current_session_token. Residual: bridge outlives a revoked parent by up to 30 s (predicate migration), deployment log controls remain an operations gate.

entries.defect: Narrowed: the grievance document, search, intelligence and collaborator-access paths (9 routes, 3 services) no longer derive case access from seniority; they use ownership, creation or an active assignment, and the legacy-service shortcuts were deleted. Collaborator access can now be granted only by the case's primary owner (previously any steward or above could grant themselves or anyone access to any case). Remaining: the member directory still scopes by role level (lib/members/directory-access.ts; names and contacts only), and the CUPE role matrix still defines case_read_any. CLAIMS READ SCOPE CLOSED: caseReadScope no longer grants a tenant-wide read to chief steward, officer or admin. A member reads their own cases, staff the cases assigned to them, and the holder of a live, expiring, administrator-granted `cases` triage designation additionally sees UNASSIGNED cases so they can be assigned (lib/triage/designations.ts, platform 0014, RLS 0021). Proven on in-process PostgreSQL (own, assigned, designation, expiry, revocation, other organization, wrong scope) and on real PostgreSQL 16 as the runtime role with row-level security, in both audit modes. DELIBERATE CONSEQUENCE: until kernel supervisory mandates are issued (they need the institutionally adopted issuance rules), nobody can read other staff's assigned cases except the assignee; a designation holder can assign unassigned cases but cannot take over an assigned one. Platform roles (app_owner, system_admin, platform_lead, platform_admin) map to no claims-case role, so platform administration no longer reads or exports customer claims (ratchet PLATFORM-ROLE-CASE-PROMOTION). KERNEL ADOPTION, FIRST DOMAIN (grievance case access and primary-representative assignment: PATCH /api/grievances/[id]/assign now assigns or reassigns through assignPrimaryRepresentative, i.e. kernel assignCase or reassignCase under the issuer's case:assign authority and the adopted rule, with the legacy column written only as a compatibility mirror for unmigrated readers and the previous representative taken from the kernel; proven on PGlite with real kernel storage: unauthorized issuer, ineligible assignee, first assignment, idempotent repeat, reassignment, refused reassignment leaving the incumbent, audit chain): lib/authority/store/route-adapter.ts is the one adapter between a request transaction and enforceAuthority; lib/services/case-access-service.ts now answers getEffectiveCaseAccess, collaborator grant and revoke, and the roster ONLY from kernel decisions and governed relationships (grants are assignCase under the adopted case_assignment rule, audited by the kernel in the same transaction); the 11 callers (grievance read, access, documents, status, intelligence, related documents, search, document authorization) keep their interface and no longer have a legacy source. The pre-kernel grievance_case_access_assignments table is retired as an authority source (ratchet RETIRED-CASE-ACCESS-TABLE at zero; the kernel case loader no longer derives collaborators from it, and a pglite test proves a legacy row grants nothing), list scopes use live non-recused kernel relationships as a pre-filter only, and member offboarding ends relationships through the membership check the kernel makes on every decision. Proven on PGlite with real kernel storage (rank, the union_rep_id column, foreign organization, missing case, ineligible grantee, self grant, primary owner, expiry terms, revocation, audit chain); the combined suite passes on fresh real PostgreSQL 16. NOT done: the claims/cases (CUPE action enforcer, caseReadScope), documents, messaging, directory, finance and governance routes still use their own policy helpers; the kernel cannot grant anything in production until kernel storage (0013, 0020) is qualified and the issuance rules are adopted, so until then only the case creator and nothing else reads a case through this path (deliberate fail-closed). Earlier text: Not done: routing these legacy services through the kernel (kernel storage is applied nowhere in production).

entries.capability: Django-created relations are stubs without defaults
entries.defect: Found on real PostgreSQL: relations created by the Django lineage have no column defaults (id, created_at, updated_at, status) and several are bare stubs (messages, in_app_notifications, and the 4-column payments already recorded). Drizzle inserts that rely on database defaults, and code written against the Drizzle shape, fail on the canonical schema while passing on mirrored in-process tables. Fixed for message_threads, messages and in_app_notifications in platform 0014. CENSUS (db/__tests__/canonical-schema-census.postgres.test.ts, baseline ue-canonical-schema-census.json, measured on fresh PostgreSQL 16 after Django migrate and the approved bootstrap): 500 Drizzle table declarations cannot be served as declared by the real schema: 63 relations absent, 425 with columns the declaration selects or writes that the relation lacks, and 173 with a NOT NULL column without default that the declaration cannot supply, so inserts fail. Examples: dues_transactions lacks 22 declared columns (amount, status, period, processor fields), so the dues payment and settlement paths cannot run on this lineage; payments lacks 20 more. The census is a ratchet (no table may gain a defect). First repair: platform 0016 adds the nullable org_id mirror the documents declaration selects and the external upload writes (constrained to equal organization_id), which took the baseline from 500 to 499 and fixed 24 write sites. Platform 0017 gives dues_transactions the ledger shape its services declare (22 columns, defaults, a period-order check; a populated stub is refused rather than given invented amounts), proven with the real Drizzle declarations as the runtime role (defaults, tenant isolation, period check), baseline 498. Two competing Drizzle declarations of dues_transactions still exist (domains/finance/dues.ts, 30 columns, and dues-transactions-schema.ts, 27) and both are now served. Registry classification of the census entries: 162 LATENT_UNREACHABLE (retire candidates, no repair needed), 116 CONTAINED_NO_AUTHORITY, about 180 live tenant, parent, user or multi-party relations, 23 global reference and 12 system-only. Platform 0018 (generated by apps/union-eyes/scripts/generate-stub-evolution.ts, reviewed) evolves 47 live relations with at least three application write sites (calendar, grievance deadlines and transitions, notifications, campaigns, remittances, signatures, voting, external-system mirrors and others) additively, with NOT NULL only on empty relations and no keys or RLS; every evolved relation is selected through its Drizzle declaration as the runtime role on real PostgreSQL 16; baseline 451. Platform 0019 (second generated tranche, 77 relations with a runtime privilege and at least one read or write site) also gives Django's base-model id, created_at and updated_at a database default where the declarations do not supply them, which was the only blocker for 46 relations; the generator now also handles enum arrays and array defaults and REFUSES a table whose enum name is declared with different members elsewhere. Every evolved relation the runtime can SELECT is selected through its declaration on real PostgreSQL 16 (insert-only relations are skipped by design); baseline 374. Platform 0020 (third generated tranche) evolves 23 more live, referenced relations (organizing, settlements, surveys, polls, federations, arbitrations, safety and others), baseline 351; fresh PostgreSQL 16 smoke as the runtime role passes. EVERY remaining entry is now classified with its proof in ue-canonical-schema-disposition.json (checked complete by db/__tests__/canonical-schema-disposition.test.ts): 103 RETIRE_DECLARATION (latent-unreachable by the registry with no reference outside the schema folder; an attempt to delete them showed they are still named by foreign keys and relations in the schema folder, so retirement needs that schema reworked together and was reverted), 59 VERIFY_UNREACHABLE_THEN_RETIRE (latent but referenced), 116 CONTAINED_DENY_ALL, 23 GLOBAL_REFERENCE_SHAPE, 12 SYSTEM_ONLY_SHAPE, 10 CREATE_RELATION_REQUIRED (declared relation absent), 15 LIVE_UNREFERENCED, 7 INDIVIDUAL_DECISION, 4 REGISTRY_GAP, 2 SEPARATE_DATABASE. Honest status: this is classification, not closure; 351 entries remain unresolved. Earlier tranche text: NOT evolved: enum-name collisions needing an individual decision (consent_records, user_consents, alert_rules, social_campaigns, integration_sync_log; campaign_status was resolved in 0018 in favour of campaigns), automation_rules (no runtime privilege), knowledge_base (needs the pgvector extension, a separate prerequisite), tables with a NOT NULL column the declaration cannot supply, tables with no write site, and the 162 unreachable ones. Foreign keys and indexes are not created by this path, and insert paths beyond the select smoke still need per-route real-schema tests; the real-schema probe also showed that documents has many required columns without defaults, so any insert must supply them. Every relation still needs a decision: evolve the stub through a platform migration, or retire the declaration and its callers; the census does not say which routes are reachable.
entries.securityImplications: Features reported as working may be unrunnable on the deployed schema; they fail closed rather than open.
entries.requiredImplementation: Census DONE and ratcheted. Next: rank the 500 entries by reachable write path, then per relation evolve the stub through a platform migration (as 0014 and 0015) or retire it, and add a real-schema test per write path; shrink the baseline as each is fixed. CONTINUATION 7: Census 351 -> 235: 116 dead Drizzle declarations (LATENT_UNREACHABLE, no importer outside db/schema) retired with evidence; regenerated against fresh native PostgreSQL 16, no entry added or changed. 46 candidates kept (live importers, dead-module-only importers, source-scanning certifications, frozen document files) and listed in the checkpoint-7 document. Remaining 235: 116 CONTAINED_DENY_ALL, 59-ish verify/retire, individual decisions and create-relation-required items.

entries.capability: Atomic audit for governed mutations
entries.defect: appendMandatoryAudit returns false outside Canonical V2, so mutations that ignored the result were silently unaudited, and governance routes audited over a separate connection that cannot roll the mutation back. Converted to persistAtomicAudit (canonical ledger, else an audit_logs insert in the same transaction, no separate-connection fallback): governance approvals (including denials), policy lifecycle transitions, board packets, policy templates, council elections, reserved matters and the Class B vote; claim and case creation, case assignment, notes, transition and escalation to grievance, grievance creation, intake submission and bulk import rows, steward assignment, status change, priority override, intake conversion, document upload, collaborator access grant and revocation (now decided and audited in one transaction), workbench assignment, dispatch request and assignment, case evidence upload and delete (the stored object is removed only after the record and its audit commit), grievance clause link, representation-authority lifecycle and external document grant lifecycle, organization membership create, document upload and download, admin membership actions, and dues payment and settlement. Proven on in-process PostgreSQL: commit together, rollback when the audit write fails, and independence under concurrent transactions. REMAINING: a few files still call the best-effort writers (auditLog, auditDataMutation, auditSecurityEvent), including recommend-steward (a read-only recommendation, no mutation). A scan of every non-test file under app/api and lib now finds only 13 files that used a separate-connection mutation writer; this pass converted notification preferences, employer communications and contacts, CBA intelligence sources, the document repository upload and label change, duplicate-group resolution, ingestion retry (now all-or-nothing, replacing a per-record partial-success loop) and the grievance deadline confirm, override and supersede lifecycle (which also gained the organization scope it lacked: grievance_deadlines has no organization column, and the three updates matched on the deadline id alone). Remaining: the supplementary summary audits in case intake and bulk import, denial-path audits, and recommend-steward; the supplementary summary audits in case intake and bulk import are not authority-bearing because each claim is audited atomically inside createClaim (the denial-path auditLog calls in converted routes are intentionally kept); each is a governed mutation and must be converted with its tests.
entries.securityImplications: A governed mutation, including an approval, could commit without its durable audit record.
entries.requiredImplementation: Convert every authority-bearing mutation to persistAtomicAudit inside its own transaction; ratchet CASE-MUTATION-BEST-EFFORT-AUDIT holds the converted routes and services at zero; extend it as the remaining callers convert.

entries.capability: Mutations identified only by a client-supplied id

In request context db is routed to the caller's tenant transaction, so row-level security still bounds them; in system context, cron, webhook and job code it does not. Fixed so far with the predicate in the statement itself: deadline confirm, override and supersede, extension request and approval, completion and escalation (shared predicate lib/deadline-engine/deadline-scope.ts, proven against another organization on PGlite), shared clause library update and delete, ingestion retry, and grievance assign, status and convert.

The scanner is textual: it does not follow a predicate built in a helper, and it does not cover raw SQL. CONTINUATION 7: Unscoped UPDATE/DELETE candidates 276 -> 26 (lib/services/platform workers, public callbacks, webhooks, cron, parent-owned writes now carry an organization predicate in the statement or bind through the parent row; cross-tenant proofs on PGlite). The 26 left: 7 latent services/financial-service (unreachable), 2 platform-global pre-claim workbook writes (claim token / signed Stripe reference), 2 pilot_applications sites bound by compare-and-set the scanner cannot see, and 15 user-scoped location/geofence/privacy/clc-sync rows with no organization column (bound by user id; classification review needed). Defects found while threading and fixed: cross-organization calendar/clause/device/exception access and a mass-assignable organizationId in GraphQL updateClaim.

entries.capability: Generic CRUD routes authorise by role floor only
entries.defect: About 310 route files expose 88 tables through crudRoutes with an organization filter and a role floor. A steward could read every claim and grievance in the tenant, and PATCH any column of claims, organization members, organizations, dues, remittances and similar records, through routes that audit nothing; admin-labelled stub routes (alerts, PKI, segments, roles) were generic writes on organization_members. Each table behind a generic route is now classified: DENIED (documents, integration keys, OAuth providers, external accounts, security events, poll votes, WCB claims, employment history, pending profiles), SUBJECT_OWNED (consents and data-subject requests, usable only through an owner-scoped route), OWN_ROWS_READ (claims, grievances and deadlines are readable only as the caller's own rows at every role, no generic write), READ_ONLY (identity, organization, money and federation tables), and OPERATIONAL (the remainder, role floor and tenant scope). A table with no entry is DENIED. Every remaining generic write (create, update, soft and hard delete) now runs in one tenant transaction with its durable audit record (field names only, never values), and is refused without an organization and acting user. REMAINING: the READ_ONLY identity and money tables need their dedicated authority-checked write routes; the stub routes mislabelled over organization_members should be retired.
entries.securityImplications: Seniority could read another member's case and change identity, money, consent or credential records through the generic interface.
entries.requiredImplementation: Keep the classification complete (the test fails when a table gains a generic route without an entry); prove the audited write on real PostgreSQL; retire or replace the mislabelled stub routes.

entries.capability: Route-coverage manifest and adoption ratchets
entries.defect: No artifact recorded, for each of the 968 app/api routes, how it authenticates, what bounds its data, whether its writes are audited atomically or whether the authority kernel decides it. The manifest now does (textual classification, with one import hop followed for audit evidence), and three ratchets hold it: a mutating route with no authentication mechanism must be in a documented public allowlist (8 today; each now carries a control the ratchet asserts: the staging-proof route answers only an image built for staging, by build-time NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV, so a production build can never answer a proof request whatever its runtime variables say; workbook, contact, whop and assessment routes use the shared public-intake guard (per-client limit that refuses when the limiter is unavailable outside development, a 16 KB body cap, strict JSON); the auth request routes are limited per IP by the proxy; capability-token routes are limited before any lookup); the route-level audit gap may not grow (baseline shrinks as routes convert); and the kernel-adoption backlog for case, claim, document and message mutations may not grow. The scan found the emergency routes returning 200 with an invented declaration, an activated break-glass state, audit and notification claims and fabricated preparedness and compliance figures, persisting nothing, with recovery callable by any authenticated user; activate, recovery and dashboard now return 501 (capability UE-EMERGENCY-DECLARATION). entries.securityImplications: Routes with no recorded authority basis, and routes that assert operational facts that are not true.
entries.requiredImplementation: Shrink apps/union-eyes baselines in docs/union-eyes/convergence/register/ue-route-coverage-baselines.json to zero by converting each listed route; regenerate the manifest with scripts/generate-route-manifest.ts.

entries.capability: Voting-session and council-election integrity
entries.defect: A steward could PATCH a voting session to any status (reopening a closed election), rewrite its title and dates after it opened, and DELETE it in any state, including after ballots were cast; the service updated and deleted by session id alone, and the evidence pack was best-effort. The council-election item route let a governance-role caller rewrite candidates, winners, totals and the verifying auditor of a certified result with no audit. Now: a status lifecycle (closed and cancelled are terminal), terms locked once a session opens, deletion only of an empty draft, organization predicates on the session writes, and update and audit committed in one tenant transaction; certified election results are locked except for recording a dispute, and creation and update are audited in the same system transaction. INSTITUTIONAL DECISIONS OPEN: whether an election officer may extend an open session's closing time, and what independent procedure may correct a certified result. REMAINING: voting options, voter eligibility and proxy changes on an opened session, ballot casting and session creation audit, and the elections vote route.
entries.securityImplications: An election's lifecycle, terms, ballots or certified results could be changed or destroyed by a role floor.
entries.requiredImplementation: Apply the same lifecycle lock to options, eligibility and proxy routes; add atomic audit to ballot casting and session creation; adopt an institutional procedure for extension and correction.

entries.capability: Claims, cases, documents and grievance mutations decided by the authority kernel
entries.defect: The claims model (the cases API) authorised by role rank: requireCaseAction asked a CUPE role matrix, caseReadScope read own, assigned_to (a mutable mirror column) or, for any staff role, a triage designation, and history visibility followed role (admin saw everything). The kernel loader now resolves a claim by claim_id (creator = the member who filed it), findReadableCase decides one kernel action per operation on the transaction that does the work (read, read_internal, comment, write_notes, transition, close, assign, upload_evidence, modify_document, export_sealed_evidence), returns null (404) when the caller cannot read the case and a recorded 403 when they can read but not act, and carries the decision's visibility (internal or member_visible) into history filtering and the redaction of internal assessments. Case and workbench assignment record the governed kernel assignment (assignPrimaryRepresentative) and keep assigned_to only as a compatibility mirror; self-assignment is refused by the kernel. Opening a case is a capacity on the canonical membership (member, handler, bulk), not a rank. A triage designation lists the unassigned queue as metadata only (claim id and number, type, status, priority, dates). Grievance convert, priority override and steward recommendation are kernel decisions inside their transactions; grievance create and import use capacity. Document version append now needs the uploader or the kernel's modify-document decision on the linked grievance, and commits with its audit; external document upload is audited atomically. Ten generic-CRUD stub routes over claims and grievances and six legacy documents routes (role-ranked, behind LEGACY_DOCUMENT_API_ENABLED) are retired to 501. Message routes are governed by the thread-participant and thread-assignment policy (the kernel has no message resource) and external matter routes by the external representation authority; both are recorded as subordinate policies with their own proofs. Intake now always files for the authenticated member in every deployment mode. Proven on PGlite with the real kernel storage and real findReadableCase (lib/cases/kernel-claims.pglite.test.ts, 21 tests): creator, assignment, reassignment, revocation, recusal, mandate scope, rank, foreign tenant, designation, history and detail projection. REMAINING: no kernel action exists for creating a case, so creation is a membership capacity; triage designation holders cannot yet route a case (kernel assignment needs an issuance source for designations, an institutional adoption); the kernel grants nothing in production until issuance rules are adopted and storage 0013 and 0020 are qualified; claims carry no unit or territory fact, so scoped supervisory mandates cannot match a claim; real-PostgreSQL qualification of the claims path (the earlier case-read-scope suite was retired with the role model); UI components for status and workflow still call retired stubs and OCR upload has no canonical equivalent.
entries.securityImplications: Seniority, a mutable column or a triage designation could read or change another member's case.
entries.requiredImplementation: Add the real-PostgreSQL claims proof; adopt an issuance source for triage routing; migrate the status, workflow and OCR UI to the canonical routes.

entries.capability: Authority-bearing mutations commit with their audit record
entries.defect: Mutating routes recorded no audit, a best-effort one, or reported success for a change that matched nothing. Converted to persistAtomicAudit on the transaction that does the work (a failed audit write fails and rolls back the change; a change that matches no row is a 404 with no audit): governance golden-share issue, reserved-matter vote recording, policy draft, snapshot, conflict resolution, replay start, mission audit, policy rule; dues manual match, reject, arrears payment, remittance update, payment plan; organization create, update, archive and settings; SSO provider creation; voting session creation; governance election sessions (now drafts in the caller's own organization that follow the session lifecycle: the route took organization and status from the body, listed every organization's sessions and let PATCH/DELETE bypass the terms lock and cancel closed elections); board-packet update and archive (a packet cannot be set to distributed outside its distribution workflow); correspondence (every transition commits its status change, hash-chained trail entry and platform audit, only lands if the letter is still in the status it was decided against, and the drafter cannot approve their own letter); signature documents (viewing was open to every member of the organization and voiding to anyone who could view; viewing is now the sender and the signers, voiding the sender, a signature no longer lands on a voided or completed document or over an existing one); committee workspace (every route loaded and changed meetings, minutes, attendance, action items and documents by id alone, outside any tenant context; each route now proves the committee and child belong to the caller's organization and to each other, and approved minutes cannot be rewritten or re-approved); pension (any member could list every member's benefit claims, contributions and T4A records, submit a claim for anyone with any status including approved or paid, and a steward could delete a plan or rewrite trustee-meeting minutes; reads are now the caller's own records, organization-wide only for the pension administrator, a claim is filed for oneself as pending, tax records cannot be marked filed, and administration needs the financial role; because the administrator is currently only the financial role, an organization administrator without it sees only their own pension records until the trustee-administration authority is adopted); exit interviews (create, edit, submit, review, publish, governance and attachments are atomic; the author cannot review their own interview and only a reviewed interview publishes; attachments, including transcripts, of an unpublished interview were readable by any member and could be added to a published one; the storage-host check accepted look-alike hosts); PKI signing workflows (an administrator could read, advance or cancel any organization's workflow by id, advance one past signatures not yet given, and sign into another organization's workflow; workflows are now scoped to the organization and have no manual advance) and the representation protocol (save, legacy submission, approval and reset commit with their audit record and approval judges a locked row); subscription pause and resume; member deactivation, deletion and reactivation (deactivate/delete audit commits with the local status change and records an incomplete offboarding as a failure; reactivation records its attempt before granting and grants nothing if the attempt cannot be recorded). Platform-auth invite creation, organization auth-policy update and MFA disable previously swallowed audit failures and now fail with the operation; the manifest counts those services only while a ratchet proves the guarantee. Kernel case-assignment mutators are counted as audited while the store proves its relationship writes record an audit row on the same executor. Ballot-casting routes are deliberately unaudited per ballot (G12) and pinned by a ratchet; the ballot error log no longer carries the member or the option. Two authority defects were closed in passing: an organization administrator can no longer change an organization parent affiliation or status (platform authority is required; resubmitting current values is allowed), and an SSO provider cannot map groups to roles a tenant administrator cannot assign. REMAINING: see ROUND 2 below for the current baseline (was 271, then 192); platform-wide finance, billing, correspondence and signature routes, committees, pension, ICRA/OCRA, exit interviews and AI routes are still unconverted; denial-path audit in a separate transaction is applied route by route; the privacy consent ledger and reconciliation engine runs delegate to services whose own audit has not been proven; ballot timestamps (votes.cast_at) can still be correlated with participation records, which is an institutional decision on timestamp granularity; retiree consent to index an exit interview is recorded by an administrator on the retiree's behalf (the grantor is recorded), and whether the data subject must give it themselves is a privacy-officer decision. ROUND 2: finance and platform operations (dues remittance, upload, issues, reminder, auto-match, setup-intent, calculate; payments checkout ownership, idempotent success and failure; billing subscriptions; admin billing cycles, case ingest, PKI sign and verify and cancel; employer-execution prepare, approve, execute, remittance and replay with three-person separation of duties and row locks), the AI, CBA, clause-library, precedents and bargaining routes, notifications, members, privacy, GDPR, communications, integrations, satisfaction, targets, SCIM, social media, rewards, location, pilot, workbook, ICRA claim, MFA enrolment, onboarding, calendar sync and cron routes. Non-database effects use performAuditedOperation (intent recorded first; the operation is skipped if that fails). Routes that only compute or read over POST are pinned (COMPUTE_ONLY, with a ratchet that checks they hold no write); writes that cannot be attributed to an actor and organization (public pseudonymous intake, capability-token assessment flows, anonymous telemetry, cron-secret platform jobs) are pinned EXEMPT_UNATTRIBUTABLE with the control that bounds each, verified by test. Authority defects closed include: payment checkout for another member's transaction; a caller-supplied Stripe customer; commercial terms editable through the subscription PATCH; any steward approving and sealing payroll; remittances overwritten at any status; pilot events attributed to a body-named user and organization; any organization administrator seeding or wiping tenant data; a verifier approving their own verification; PKI verification across organizations and signing under another person's identity; cross-tenant clause, CBA, bargaining-note and RAG reads; unscoped GraphQL CRUD (retired); a member reading or cancelling another member's history, survey or redemption; CSV import granting elevated roles; SCIM provisioning into any organization; and forged compliance audit rows. REMAINING: the audit-gap baseline is 1 (icra/report/[assessmentId]/review, where a shared cron secret authorises a human review with a self-asserted reviewer role: an institutional decision); platform migration 0021 (UNQUALIFIED, not applied to any clone or live database) adds the payroll-run executor columns and the unique indexes on remittance runs per payroll run and timesheet batches per file and period, and refuses existing duplicates; PKI signing now requires the document to be the one the organization's workflow was opened for and gdpr/cookie-consent is rate limited per client; cba-intelligence data is platform-wide with no tenant column; copilot conversations are not user-scoped; a deployment with a single platform administrator cannot approve commercial terms or correct an organization binding (independent approval);
entries.securityImplications: An authority-bearing change could succeed with no durable record, or report success while the record failed.
entries.requiredImplementation: Decide the review-route authority (icra/report review); qualify platform migration 0021 on a credentialed clone; decide ballot timestamp granularity.
